t: For Xiaomi phones, this mechanism exists, but it is not triggered on unlocking.  There is a partition in the device with the name persist, which holds the sensor configuration and some device-independent identifiers, certificates, and other sensitive blobs. The partition is in read-write ext4 format, which means that it is extremely vulnerable to corruption when it is written to, or when it is full. Once the files in it are corrupted, Xiaomi's unique protect mechanism is triggered and the TEE will permanently self-destruct (and relock will not restore it). Xiaomi also acknowledged the existence of this mechanism in its recent BootLoader unlocking questionnaire. TWRP, Magisk, and ROMs may all write to it (for Magisk, you can check if it uses the partition in the logs of the installation; for TWRP, it's usually the .twrps configuration, but it's unbelievable that some versions even output logs to it). When the TEE is corrupted, you cannot get STRONG PI level.
